title: Parked vs. In Transport
citation: NJTR-1 Crash Report Manual (2023), Appendix: General Questions
key_points: In transport: on the roadway (moving or stopped), or moving anywhere in or outside the trafficway.
Parked: not moving and completely off the travel lanes. If any part of the vehicle or its load sticks into the roadway, it's in transport.
In a lane that allows parking only at certain times, a parked car counts as in transport while parking is banned.

faq.a: A car stopped at the curb whose driver opens a door into traffic; a truck on the shoulder with only its mirror over the line; any vehicle stopped on the shoulder, median or roadside; at a gas pump; in a driveway; in a metered space even if the meter ran out.

Any vehicle driving on the shoulder, median or roadside; a parked car that rolls away with no brake set; a car stopped with two tires in the lane; a tractor trailer with its load over the edge line; a van left in a travel lane during a rush-hour no-parking period; a delivery truck stopped in a "no parking any time" zone; a police car on patrol or stopped in the road at a scene; a school bus stopped in a lane with its lights on; a car pulling away from a gas pump; a moving car in a private driveway; an ATV on a trail.

faq.q: Is a work vehicle doing road work in transport?
faq.a: No, not while it's doing construction, maintenance or utility work in the work zone (for example, a bucket truck working on lines, a line-painting truck, a paving roller, or a highway plow clearing snow as road maintenance). It is in transport when driving between work sites.
